params.body:
Closes #969

## What was wrong

A vehicle created with "on Stocklist within N months" stored its **start date** as start + N months. `OwnStockService::finalizeCreate` called `addMonths()` on the mutable `Carbon` it then also saved as `available_start_date`. The publication date written on creation was right, but the sheet showed "Op Stocklist vanaf" as start + 2N, and the next save of the sheet (`finalizeEdit`) recomputed the publication date from the shifted start, so the car went on Stocklist N months later than chosen.

`finalizeEdit` already used `->copy()`; this does the same in `finalizeCreate`. The favourite-date comparison right below now also compares against the real start date.

## Test

`VehicleFormSaveTest::test_a_new_vehicle_with_a_delay_keeps_its_start_date_and_adds_the_months_once` creates a vehicle with a 2-month delay through the sheet, checks the stored start and publication dates, the "on Stocklist from" line, and that a second save does not move the date. It fails on `main`, passes here. Full suite: 3024 tests OK; PHPStan clean on the changed file.

## Not in this PR

Vehicles already created this way still carry a shifted `available_start_date` (and, once saved again, a shifted publication date). Correcting them is a data decision and is left out on purpose.
params.title: Keep a new vehicle's Stocklist start date instead of saving it with the delay added
